question: How can automated, open-ended function-description methods be compared when real neural components lack known ground-truth explanations, and does interactive LM-driven experimentation outperform description from fixed exemplars?

key_findings.claim: FIND turns automated interpretation into a ground-truthed black-box system-identification problem spanning symbolic, numeric, semantic, and factual behavior.
key_findings.evidence: The released suite includes 1,000 numeric functions and 1,000 string functions plus synthetic Vicuna-backed entity and factual-relation modules. Procedural operators add composition, additive noise, local domain corruption, approximation by a two-layer MLP, and multi-concept selectivity, so an interpreter must recover more than a single global label.

key_findings.claim: A GPT-4 Automated Interpretability Agent is the strongest uninitialized interactive baseline, but it remains unreliable on exact function recovery and often learns only global behavior.
key_findings.evidence: Table 2 reports GPT-4 AIA success of 0.33 on numeric code, 0.23 on exact string code, 0.82 on string language unit tests, 0.56 on entities, and 0.78 on relations. GPT-3.5 reaches 0.12/0.13/0.66/0.39/0.37 and both Llama-2 variants are at or near zero for exact code. The authors summarize the best agent as inadequately describing 48% of functions and show that small corrupted subdomains are commonly missed.

key_findings.claim: Supplying a small targeted exemplar set before interaction is more useful than unconstrained agent search, especially for narrow semantic concepts.
key_findings.evidence: For GPT-4 entity modules, fixed-exemplar MILAN rises from the uninitialized AIA's 0.56 to 0.89, while relations shift from 0.78 to 0.74. Combining the same two positive and eight distractor exemplars with subsequent AIA probing reaches 0.89 on entities and 0.92 on relations; GPT-3.5 similarly improves to 0.88 and 0.68. The paper traces the gap to agents initially trying generic words that do not expose specific entities.

key_findings.claim: The learned unit-test evaluator agrees with human judgments on the tested semantic modules, but its scoring protocol systematically under-penalizes missing local details.
key_findings.evidence: On ground-truth descriptions, the fine-tuned Vicuna evaluator scores 0.956/0.981/0.998 for strings/entities/relations versus 0.900/0.964/0.952 for GPT-4. On 25 entity and 25 relation functions, its per-function interpretation scores correlate with three human raters at Spearman 0.904 and 0.89. Yet the appendix notes that interpreters almost always miss relation corruptions and can still score well because only two of ten representative tests probe the corrupted region.

key_findings.claim: The synthetic neural modules are useful controlled targets but are themselves imperfect simulations of real learned components.
key_findings.evidence: Entity modules are prompted Vicuna functions whose mean association score is 0.85 for ten human labels per entity and 0.08 for distractors; factual relation modules answer their intended mapping with mean accuracy 91.2%. Thus benchmark errors can reflect the Vicuna function implementation as well as the interpreter, unlike explicit numeric and string programs.

method.core_idea: Evaluate automated interpreters against procedurally generated black-box functions whose true implementation and human-legible description are known, then score both executable reconstructions and natural-language explanations on held-out behavior.
method.mechanism: FIND packages each function as an independently callable Python script. Numeric and string tasks instantiate atomic operations and controlled compositions, noise, corruptions, or MLP approximations; Vicuna-13B implements semantic entity and Wikidata-derived relation modules. Interpreters either receive fixed exemplars, autonomously choose queries through a Python tool, or combine both. Numeric and string code is executed on held-out inputs, while a separately fine-tuned Vicuna evaluator maps language descriptions to representative input-output unit tests. GPT-4, GPT-3.5, and Llama-2 baselines are compared across the same categories.
assumptions: Describing these procedurally generated black-box functions measures capabilities necessary for describing real neural components, even though it is not sufficient evidence of real-model interpretability.
Numeric NMSE below 0.1, exact string execution, and three-way language unit tests correspond to useful function descriptions.
The ground-truth descriptions generated from source code and the fine-tuned Vicuna evaluator do not leak benchmark answers into the tested interpreter models.
Vicuna reliably implements prompted entity and factual functions well enough that the resulting black boxes have stable intended semantics.
A language description that selects representative held-out behavior is an adequate proxy for the local and global fidelity needed by downstream users.

techniques.role: Generates many known functions while controlling composition, approximation, observation noise, and localized corruption.
Lets an LM agent choose function inputs, inspect outputs, revise hypotheses, and stop with code and a natural-language description.
Tests generated code on held-out inputs using normalized error or exact-match execution rather than judging its surface form.
Scores a language explanation by asking an evaluator to distinguish representative ground-truth behavior from same-category distractors.
Seeds interactive interpretation with two relevant and eight distractor examples to overcome weak broad-search behavior.
Compares automated unit-test scores with repeated human judgments on semantic function subsets.

evaluations.setting: Uninitialized automated interpretation over numeric, string, entity, and relation FIND functions
evaluations.metric: Success rate: numeric NMSE below 0.1, string exact code match, or language unit-test score above chance
evaluations.result: GPT-4 scores 0.33 numeric, 0.23 string-code, 0.82 string-language, 0.56 entity, and 0.78 relation

evaluations.setting: Synthetic entity and relation modules with fixed exemplars and optional subsequent interaction
evaluations.result: GPT-4 AIA+MILAN scores 0.89 on entities and 0.92 on relations
evaluations.baseline: Uninitialized GPT-4 AIA 0.56/0.78 and non-interactive MILAN 0.89/0.74

evaluations.setting: Ground-truth descriptions of all string/entity/relation functions with ten representative tests per function
evaluations.metric: Evaluator accuracy in a three-way representative-versus-distractor choice

evaluations.setting: Twenty-five entity and twenty-five relation functions, ten unit tests per function, with three Mechanical Turk raters per task
evaluations.metric: Per-function Spearman correlation between human and Vicuna-evaluator scores
evaluations.result: rho=0.904 for entities and rho=0.89 for relations
evaluations.baseline: Both evaluators are also tested with ground-truth descriptions as a near-ceiling control

evaluations.setting: Vicuna-backed entity and factual-relation implementation audit
evaluations.metric: Association separation and factual mapping accuracy
evaluations.result: Entity scores average 0.85 on ten human-associated labels and 0.08 on distractors; relation mapping accuracy averages 91.2%
evaluations.baseline: Human-associated versus cross-entity distractor concepts, and Wikidata-derived intended relation outputs

limitations: Author-stated: FIND tests necessary but not sufficient capabilities; the decisive criterion is actionable insight about real models, which the benchmark does not evaluate.
Author-stated: the release contains only black-box tasks even though much mechanistic interpretability is white-box and concerns interactions among internal computations.
Author-stated: automated agents tend to identify global behavior while missing local corruptions, which may correspond to practically important biases or rare failure regions.
Author-stated: the unit-test evaluator is forgiving of vague descriptions and can award strong scores when an interpreter fails to mention a corrupted subdomain.

Reviewer-identified: entity and relation targets are prompt-programmed Vicuna behavior, not components that emerged through model training; their 91.2% relation fidelity introduces label noise into the benchmark itself.
Reviewer-identified: results depend on proprietary, versioned GPT-4/GPT-3.5 APIs and short interaction budgets, while the open Llama-2 baselines sometimes fail to execute the tool at all.
Reviewer-identified: success thresholds collapse graded accuracy into binary outcomes and the three-way language test can be passed by descriptions too coarse for intervention or safety auditing.
Reviewer-identified: exemplar initialization uses human-constructed positive concepts, so its gain does not establish that an autonomous interpreter can discover informative experiments from scratch.
failure_modes: An interpreter samples familiar generic inputs and never reaches a narrow semantic concept or rare corrupted region.
A generated description captures a function family while omitting parameters, composition order, noise distribution, or local exceptions.
A language evaluator accepts a broad label because it distinguishes one representative behavior from easy distractors, despite poor predictive fidelity elsewhere.
The synthetic module violates its prompt-programmed rule, causing a correct empirical description to disagree with the intended ground truth.
An agent hallucinates tool outputs or claims to have executed experiments, as observed for Llama-2 baselines.
A method overfits FIND's procedural grammar and fails on real learned features whose behavior is distributed, context-dependent, or causally entangled.
reusable_insights: Benchmark explanations by the new behavior they predict, not only by agreement with a reference sentence.
Include small adversarial subdomains in system-identification tasks because global fit can conceal the failures most relevant to safety and fairness.
Separate search quality from description quality by comparing fixed exemplars, autonomous probes, and exemplar-initialized interaction.
Calibrate LM judges against humans and ground-truth controls, then explicitly audit where the evaluation protocol is insensitive.
A tool-using interpretability agent benefits from experiment generators, search coverage diagnostics, and falsification policies more than from unconstrained extra dialogue alone.
Use executable reconstructions when possible; natural-language unit tests should include counterexamples targeted to every claimed clause.
open_questions: Can an interpreter adaptively prove coverage of local exceptions instead of relying on an unmeasured sample of probes?
How should FIND-like tasks expose internal activations, weights, and circuit structure while retaining ground-truth causal semantics?
Do gains on procedural functions predict successful auditing or editing of real large models under blinded prospective evaluation?
Can evaluator tests be generated directly from every atomic claim in a description, including negations and domain boundaries?
What is the performance frontier when search calls, model tokens, and human-provided exemplars are budgeted separately?

competitive_landscape.title: Natural Language Descriptions of Deep Visual Features
competitive_landscape.difference: MILAN searches for high-mutual-information language descriptions of fixed maximally activating image regions and validates them with humans and downstream audits; FIND abstracts the task into known functions and adds autonomous query selection, executable reconstruction, and controlled failure types.

competitive_landscape.title: Towards Automated Circuit Discovery for Mechanistic Interpretability
competitive_landscape.difference: ACDC automates causal edge selection in real transformer computation graphs and evaluates recovery of previously hand-discovered circuits; FIND evaluates semantic black-box description with known procedural targets and does not localize internal causal structure.

competitive_landscape.title: A Multimodal Automated Interpretability Agent
competitive_landscape.difference: MAIA equips a vision-language model with image synthesis, editing, exemplar search, and experiment logging, then tests descriptions on real vision neurons and synthetic neurons plus model-level failure discovery and mitigation; it operationalizes FIND's active-scientist idea with richer tools and more realistic targets.

competitive_landscape.title: CoSy: Evaluating Textual Explanations of Neurons
competitive_landscape.difference: CoSy conditions a generative model on a proposed visual-neuron description and compares the neuron's activation on synthesized versus control data, directly testing a real feature's predicted behavior; FIND instead uses procedurally known black boxes and representative unit tests across numeric and language domains.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: FIND is presented as a comprehensive, extensible ground-truth benchmark for open-ended automated function description and as the first demonstration of an LM interpretability agent that chooses its own experiments.
novelty_assessment.evidence: The suite combines more than two thousand procedural tasks, explicit complexity operators, code and language metrics, several agent and exemplar baselines, an open evaluator, and human calibration; the results expose large model and search-strategy gaps that small bespoke neuron-label tests did not quantify.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: Relative to MILAN and concurrent circuit automation, FIND's durable novelty is the separation of interpretation search, description, and behavioral validation on controlled functions. Subsequent MAIA and CoSy move toward richer real-neuron tools and predictive evaluation, so FIND is best treated as a unit-test layer rather than a complete benchmark of mechanistic understanding.

reviewer_notes: All 28 extracted pages were consulted, with quantitative claims checked against Table 2 and Appendix Tables A3-A4. The primary-source competitor records were checked on arXiv and OpenReview on 2026-08-23. The OpenReview page may present a browser challenge to automated clients, but its official record metadata identifies the NeurIPS 2024 poster. Statements about missed corruptions and evaluator forgiveness are author-reported; implications for safety audits are reviewer inference.
